topics.title: Completing the square and the graph

questions.stem: Consider the parabola with equation \( y = (x - 3)^2 - 4 \) in completed square form.
questions.hint: Write a full structured solution for the teacher to mark.

steps.explain: Identify the concavity by checking the sign of the leading coefficient.
Substitute \( x = 0 \) to find the y-intercept.
From the completed square form \( y = a(x - h)^2 + k \), the vertex is \( (h, k) \) and axis of symmetry is \( x = h \).
Since the vertex is below the x-axis \( (y = -4) \) and the parabola is concave up, it must cross the x-axis. Find the intercepts by setting \( y = 0 \).

questions.stem: Consider the concave-down parabola with completed square form \( y = -(x - 2)^2 + 4 \).
questions.hint: Write a full structured solution for the teacher to mark.

steps.explain: Look at the negative sign in front of the parenthetical squared term.
Substitute \( x = 0 \) to calculate the y-intercept.
Read off the vertex \( (h, k) \) from the equation form \( y = -(x - h)^2 + k \).
Since the vertex is above the x-axis \( (y = 4) \) and the parabola is concave down, it must cross the x-axis. Find the intercepts by setting \( y = 0 \).
